core_claim: Broad abiotic gradients directly and monotonically scale the fitness consequences of floral interactions.
decisive_missing_test: Manipulated abiotic gradient that reproducibly switches interaction strength across replicated Cirsium populations.

core_claim: Environmental context acts strongly at the seed-to-recruitment/population bottleneck, so the same fecundity effect can transmit or disappear depending on safe sites, disturbance and density dependence.
decisive_missing_test: Factorial focal-system test linking seed output to recruitment across manipulated microsite/disturbance or density contexts.

core_claim: Pollinator dependence and realized pollen limitation are decoupled by autonomous selfing, donor spacing, flowering synchrony and local density.
decisive_missing_test: Within-system factorial test of pollinator exclusion/supplementation across assurance contexts with final seed fitness.

core_claim: When pollination service is above an assurance threshold, antagonist avoidance/protection should contribute more consistently to marginal fitness than extra attraction; pollinator-facing benefits should re-emerge below that threshold.
decisive_missing_test: Same populations and same fitness scale measuring marginal pollination benefit and marginal antagonist cost across a gradient of pollination assurance.

core_claim: Floral modules can mitigate mutualist-antagonist conflict by partitioning exposure in time, space or sensory channels rather than settling at a static compromise.
decisive_missing_test: Cirsium manipulation showing unchanged total visitation but shifted timing/effective contacts or enemy exposure and higher reproductive fitness.

core_claim: Different capitulum modules may act on different ecological gates and vary semi-independently, but a common-lability full model remains viable.
decisive_missing_test: Ancestry-controlled multivariate field data showing module-specific trait->interaction/protection->fitness paths and comparing shared versus module-specific random-effect structures.
